params.body:
Every merge to main currently produces TWO Forge deploys: the merge itself, and the commit
`release.yml` pushes back to main to rewrite a version badge in the README. Each of those is a full
`composer install`, `npm ci` and vite build, and each opens a window in which `current` still runs
the old code against the freshly written shared manifest (R P1-1.22). That is what a badge costs.

So the workflow now pushes a tag and nothing else. What it drops:

- the badge-rewriting step and its push to main,
- the `if:` guard that existed only to stop the workflow re-triggering on its own badge commit,
- `release-badge.yml`, which wrote the same commit and, since releases published with the default
  `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not start other workflows, had never once run.

The version is still handed out on every merge and still published as a release; it is simply read
from the releases page instead of from a badge. Which code actually runs remains the question
`/.well-known/build.json` answers, and it carries the commit.

`EveryDeployIsAVersionTest` is rewritten rather than trimmed: two of its cases pinned the badge
commit and the guard against it, so they are replaced by one that pins the opposite, that the
release pushes nothing to main. R P1-1.23 is updated with the reason.
params.title: One merge is one deploy: the release stops pushing a badge to main
